name: Achernar
description: A fast-spinning Be star 43 parsecs away, eight times the Sun's width, with a companion on a seven-year orbit.

radius.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: radius of A 8.14 +/- 0.26 solar radii, from the mean limb-darkened diameter 1.770 +/- 0.035 mas (Domiciano de Souza et al. 2014) and the Hipparcos parallax

mass.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: mass of A 5.99 +/- 0.60 solar masses, the orbit's total mass less B's model mass

temperature.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: Teff of A 15539 +/- 438 K

radialVelocity.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: barycentric radial velocity +10.49 +/- 0.51 km/s

distance.source: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: the Hipparcos parallax 23.39 +/- 0.57 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) the orbit is scaled with, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A fast-spinning Be star eight times the Sun's width, with a companion on a seven-year orbit.
text.introduction: VLT and VLTI followed its companion for 13 years: the orbit weighs Achernar at 5.99 solar masses, with 15,539 K at its surface.

notes: Achernar A spins so fast that it is much wider at its equator than at its poles; it is drawn as a sphere of its mean radius.
